subject: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items

messages.author: cf3b2060e1fe46a5
messages.subject: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items
parts:
I was trying to get fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) for a 4-item scale but, when I used the M2 function, I got this error: "M2 cannot be calulated since df is too low." 

Professor Chalmers then kindly provided some R code for simulations (see attachment), and from this I could get a X2 and G2. You can do the same using your "real" data simply by changing the following (i.e. write the name of your mirt model instead of "myMIRTmodel"):

attr(fscores(myMIRTmodel, method = 'EAPsum', verbose=FALSE), 'fit')

You can then use the X2 and df to derive other fit indices like CFI and TLI. Professor Chalmers described the following procedure: "You could create these statistics yourself because they are just chi^2 transformations compared to a null model (i.e., a model containing only intercepts). Just fit a model where you fix all the slopes (a1) to 0, and compute the new X2 and G2 stats for the NULL model. From there, just plug in the degrees of freedom into the CFI, TLI, RMSEA, etc and you'll have your reference fit stats."

The next version of the mirt package should be able to do this automatically (hopefully this feature will be added soon).

I thank Professor Chalmers for his kind support.

messages.author: cf3b2060e1fe46a5
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items
parts:
I used the following to calculate RMSEA:

fitX  <- attr(fscores(gmirt, method = 'EAPsum', verbose=FALSE), 'fit') 
fitX
RMSEA  <- sqrt(fitX$X2-fitX$df)/sqrt(fitX$df*(N-1))
round(RMSEA, 3)

It seems to work fine. Do you think it produces incorrect values?


With regards to the null model, I tried to fix the slopes to 0 by specifying it this way:

nullmodel <- mirt.model('F = 1-4
CONSTRAIN = (1-4, a1, 0)')

But, it doesn't seem to work, as I get the following error: "Error in p[[sel[j]]] : attempt to select less than one element"

I tried other specifications, but they seem dubious. Any suggestions?

Cheers,
Ylenio

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items
parts:
On Tue, Jun 16, 2015 at 1:14 PM, <yleni...@gmail.com> wrote:
I used the following to calculate RMSEA:

fitX  <- attr(fscores(gmirt, method = 'EAPsum', verbose=FALSE), 'fit') 
fitX
RMSEA  <- sqrt(fitX$X2-fitX$df)/sqrt(fitX$df*(N-1))
round(RMSEA, 3)

It seems to work fine. Do you think it produces incorrect values?
Calculating RMSEA is fine, but again it doesn't have exactly the same meaning because the 'parsimony' aspect of the model is not being included (the df are fixed, unlike in M2).

With regards to the null model, I tried to fix the slopes to 0 by specifying it this way:

nullmodel <- mirt.model('F = 1-4
CONSTRAIN = (1-4, a1, 0)')

But, it doesn't seem to work, as I get the following error: "Error in p[[sel[j]]] : attempt to select less than one element"

You want the FIXED and START keywords, not CONSTRAIN. The latter is for equality constraints, while the former two change whether parameters are freely estimated and what their starting values are (supported in mirt version 1.10+ only). But again, the null model will have the same df as the full model, so the CFI/TLI family of stats are not really relevant.

Phil
I tried other specifications, but they seem dubious. Any suggestions?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items
parts:
Currently, I can't suggest much that stays directly within the IRT framework. It is possible to extend the M2 statistic to create a hybrid-type model for polytomous data to fix this problem, but I haven't had the time to invest in such an endeavour. 

You may have luck switching to the SEM framework with lavaan if your items are ordered (2PL and graded), and estimate the items as ordinal, but even then I'm not convinced the problem will be solved (it's very likely that the bivariate tables will be sparse and will cause difficulties).  

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) using scales with few items
parts:
I don't really see the need for it. Item EFA can be done in mirt, and things like missing data are dealt with much better, detecting mis-fitting items, overall model fit, computing factor scores, and so on. Not to mention, it might actually be faster to do FIML estimation than limited information methods in R if the number of items is large. Plus, irt.fa seems to only support dichotomous items that have to have a 2PLM form, whereas mirt can work with a mix of dichotomous/polytomous types and with items other than the 2PL. 

But that's just my 2 cents, use whatever works best for your data.

Phil

fitX

It seems to work fine. Do you think it produces incorrect values?

Calculating RMSEA is fine, but again it doesn't have exactly the same meaning because the 'parsimony' aspect of the model is not being included (the df are fixed, unlike in M2). 
 


With regards to the null model, I tried to fix the slopes to 0 by specifying it this way:

nullmodel <- mirt.model('F = 1-4
CONSTRAIN = (1-4, a1, 0)')

But, it doesn't seem to work, as I get the following error: "Error in p[[sel[j]]] : attempt to select less than one element"

You want the FIXED and START keywords, not CONSTRAIN. The latter is for equality constraints, while the former two change whether parameters are freely estimated and what their starting values are (supported in mirt version 1.10+ only). But again, the null model will have the same df as the full model, so the CFI/TLI family of stats are not really relevant.

Phil

On Tuesday, June 16, 2015 at 5:51:26 PM UTC+1, Phil Chalmers wrote:
I believe I spoke too soon about the CFI model fit statistics and friends. This approach is not amiable to comparisons to a null model as they do not adjust for the number of estimated parameters in the model. The method is a test of absolute fit, assuming that the sample is fairly large such that the parameter estimates are stable so that their variability does not influence the large-sample approximate X^2 distribution. 

Phil

2015년 5월 27일 수요일 오전 7시 5분 4초 UTC+9, yleni...@gmail.com 님의 말:
I was trying to get fit indices (e.g. CFI, TLI, RMSEA) for a 4-item scale but, when I used the M2 function, I got this error: "M2 cannot be calulated since df is too low." 

Professor Chalmers then kindly provided some R code for simulations (see attachment), and from this I could get a X2 and G2. You can do the same using your "real" data simply by changing the following (i.e. write the name of your mirt model instead of "myMIRTmodel"):

attr(fscores(myMIRTmodel, method = 'EAPsum', verbose=FALSE), 'fit')

You can then use the X2 and df to derive other fit indices like CFI and TLI. Professor Chalmers described the following procedure: "You could create these statistics yourself because they are just chi^2 transformations compared to a null model (i.e., a model containing only intercepts). Just fit a model where you fix all the slopes (a1) to 0, and compute the new X2 and G2 stats for the NULL model. From there, just plug in the degrees of freedom into the CFI, TLI, RMSEA, etc and you'll have your reference fit stats."

The next version of the mirt package should be able to do this automatically (hopefully this feature will be added soon).

I thank Professor Chalmers for his kind support.
